title: Change Thermostat Policy: Predictive Apply & Safe Fallthrough for Cost Optimization
creator: Diego Morales
description: Design and implement a "thermostat"-style policy engine for config changes that can predict cost/latency regressions before a full apply, allow a controlled staged apply, and provide an automatic safe fallthrough path when thresholds are exceeded. This ticket focuses on the control logic, metric predicates, and state snapshot/reconciliation needed to ensure config changes (batching, caching, kernel selection, quantization profiles) can be applied with minimal customer impact and deterministic safety behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Thermostat policy accepts a config delta and returns PASS/WARN/FAIL based on predictive simulation using recent traffic distributions.
Staged apply flow: canary (1%), ramp (10%), full (100%) with automated hold/continue decisions driven by the thermostat and observable predicates.
Safe fallthrough: when a predicate trips, system applies an explicit fallthrough sequence that reverts to last-known-good config without manual intervention within 90s.
State snapshotting: pre-apply snapshot plus post-apply reconciliation logs must be stored and queryable for at least 30 days.
Integration tests that simulate KV-cache warming, batching-profile changes, and quantization toggles with representative load and assert cost/latency regressions are detected and handled.
Runbook and alerting: PagerDuty playbook created and unit/integ tests cover the most common failure modes.
implementation_notes: Predictive simulation: replay recent request distribution (seq len, prompt prefixes, batchable window) against candidate config to estimate token/sec and p99 latency delta.
Metric predicates: define relative cost delta, absolute p95/p99 latency thresholds, and error-rate increase thresholds. Use hysteresis windows to avoid noisy flips.
Thermostat scoring: combine predictive cost/latency deltas into single risk score; map score to PASS/WARN/FAIL with customizable thresholds per-customer/route.
Staged apply: implement canary tokens with request-sampling routing; allow autoscaling pause during canary if thermostat WARN persists.

Safe fallthrough behavior: instead of immediate hard rollback, apply a deterministic fallthrough that first ramps down the new config to a safe intermediate (e.g., smaller batch size) then fully revert if still unhealthy.
State reconciliation: store serialized config snapshots (metadata only) and a compact state diff. Reconciler compares live state with desired state and can force-fallthrough with idempotent ops.
Observability hooks: emit events for each policy decision, include model id, route, customer id, and deterministic reason codes to aid postmortems.
Testing: add synthetic traffic generator (long-tail seqs + short chat bursts) to CI integration tests that run the predictive sim and staged apply in a sandbox cluster.
Performance: predictive simulation should run under 2s for a route using cached histograms; if not available, fall back to conservative PASS/WARN mapping.
Compatibility: ensure fallthrough sequence works across hosted/dedicated/private deployments — use control-plane RPCs for private with retry/backoff.
updates: 2026-02-16: Initial spike and user-research notes. Identified three common failure modes for batching changes: delayed KV-cache warmup, transient p99 spikes during autoscale, and increased token cost from suboptimal kernel selection.
2026-02-22: Architecture doc shared (confluence link in links). Decided to use a hybrid approach: lightweight predictive sim + conservative defaults for unknown routes.
2026-02-28: Prototype predictive sim implemented that uses live request histograms. Local tests show it predicts cost change within 3% for stable routes.
2026-03-05: Design review with SRE and PM — Jonah asked for explicit hysteresis windows and traceable reason codes; PM requested per-customer override flags.

2026-03-09: First end-to-end sandbox run: canary applied to internal route, thermostat WARNed on KV-cache warmup; fallthrough executed to intermediate batch size; rollback fully completed in 72s. Metrics attached.
2026-03-10: Open PR created for control-plane changes and snapshot store (see links). QA scheduled for 2026-03-12.
